solution:
Any equation of the form \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\) with \(a \neq 0\) and one variable whose highest index is 2 will do. For example :

\(m^2 + 5m + 3 = 0\)

\(y^2 - 3 = 0\)

(Both have a single variable and maximum index 2, so both are quadratic equations. Any other such pair is equally correct.)

\(x^2 + 5x - 2 = 0\)

\(x\) is the only variable and its maximum index is 2, so it is already in the form \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\) with \(a = 1 \neq 0\).

\(\therefore\) It is a quadratic equation.

\(y^2 = 5y - 10\)

Rewriting, \(y^2 - 5y + 10 = 0\). \(y\) is the only variable and its maximum index is 2, with \(a = 1 \neq 0\).

\(\therefore\) It is a quadratic equation.

\(y^2 + \dfrac{1}{y} = 2\)

Multiplying throughout by \(y\) gives \(y^3 + 1 = 2y\), i.e. \(y^3 - 2y + 1 = 0\), in which the maximum index of the variable is 3, not 2.

\(\therefore\) It is not a quadratic equation.

\(x + \dfrac{1}{x} = -2\)

Multiplying throughout by \(x\) gives \(x^2 + 1 = -2x\), i.e. \(x^2 + 2x + 1 = 0\), in which \(x\) is the only variable and the maximum index is 2.

\(\therefore\) It is a quadratic equation.

\((m + 2)(m - 5) = 0\)

Expanding, \(m^2 - 5m + 2m - 10 = 0\), i.e. \(m^2 - 3m - 10 = 0\); \(m\) is the only variable with maximum index 2.

\(\therefore\) It is a quadratic equation.

\(m^3 + 3m^2 - 2 = 3m^3\)

Rearranging, \(3m^3 - m^3 - 3m^2 + 2 = 0\), i.e. \(2m^3 - 3m^2 + 2 = 0\), in which the maximum index of the variable is 3, not 2.

\(\therefore\) It is not a quadratic equation.

\(p(3 + 6p) = -5\)

\(3p + 6p^2 = -5\)

\(6p^2 + 3p + 5 = 0\)

Comparing with \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\),

\(a = 6\), \(b = 3\), \(c = 5\)

(The book prints the outer letter as a capital \(P\) and the one inside the bracket as a lowercase \(p\); both stand for the same variable, which is what its own answer \(6p^2 + 3p + 5 = 0\) requires.)

Put \(x = 1\) in \(x^2 + 4x - 5\) :

\((1)^2 + 4(1) - 5 = 1 + 4 - 5 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(x = 1\) is a root of the equation.

Put \(x = -1\) in \(x^2 + 4x - 5\) :

\((-1)^2 + 4(-1) - 5 = 1 - 4 - 5 = -8 \neq 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(x = -1\) is not a root of the equation.

So 1 is a root and \(-1\) is not.

Put \(m = 2\) in \(2m^2 - 5m\) :

\(2(2)^2 - 5(2) = 8 - 10 = -2 \neq 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(m = 2\) is not a root of the equation.

Put \(m = \dfrac{5}{2}\) in \(2m^2 - 5m\) :

\(2\left(\dfrac{5}{2}\right)^2 - 5\left(\dfrac{5}{2}\right) = 2 \times \dfrac{25}{4} - \dfrac{25}{2} = \dfrac{25}{2} - \dfrac{25}{2} = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(m = \dfrac{5}{2}\) is a root of the equation.

So \(\dfrac{5}{2}\) is a root and 2 is not.

\(x = 3\) is a root of \(kx^2 - 10x + 3 = 0\), so putting \(x = 3\) must satisfy the equation.

\(k(3)^2 - 10(3) + 3 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(9k - 30 + 3 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(9k - 27 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(9k = 27\)

\(\therefore\) \(k = 3\)

\(\dfrac{-7}{5}\) is a root of quadratic equation \(5m^2 + 2m + k = 0\)

\(\therefore\) Put \(m = \dfrac{-7}{5}\) in the equation.

\(5 \times \left(\dfrac{-7}{5}\right)^2 + 2 \times \left(\dfrac{-7}{5}\right) + k = 0\)

\(\dfrac{49}{5} + \left(\dfrac{-14}{5}\right) + k = 0\)

\(\dfrac{35}{5} + k = 0\), that is \(7 + k = 0\)

\(k = -7\)

\(x^2 - 15x + 54 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(x^2 - 9x - 6x + 54 = 0\)   (since \(-9 \times -6 = 54\) and \(-9 - 6 = -15\))

\(\therefore\) \(x(x - 9) - 6(x - 9) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \((x - 9)(x - 6) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(x - 9 = 0\) or \(x - 6 = 0\), so \(x = 9\) or \(x = 6\)

\(\therefore\) 9 and 6 are the roots of the given quadratic equation.

\(x^2 + x - 20 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(x^2 + 5x - 4x - 20 = 0\)   (since \(5 \times -4 = -20\) and \(5 - 4 = 1\))

\(\therefore\) \(x(x + 5) - 4(x + 5) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \((x + 5)(x - 4) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(x + 5 = 0\) or \(x - 4 = 0\), so \(x = -5\) or \(x = 4\)

\(\therefore\) \(-5\) and 4 are the roots of the given quadratic equation.

\(2y^2 + 27y + 13 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(2y^2 + 26y + y + 13 = 0\)   (since \(26 \times 1 = 26 = 2 \times 13\) and \(26 + 1 = 27\))

\(\therefore\) \(2y(y + 13) + 1(y + 13) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \((y + 13)(2y + 1) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(y + 13 = 0\) or \(2y + 1 = 0\), so \(y = -13\) or \(y = -\dfrac{1}{2}\)

\(\therefore\) \(-13\) and \(-\dfrac{1}{2}\) are the roots of the given quadratic equation.

\(5m^2 = 22m + 15\)

\(\therefore\) \(5m^2 - 22m - 15 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(5m^2 - 25m + 3m - 15 = 0\)   (since \(-25 \times 3 = -75 = 5 \times -15\) and \(-25 + 3 = -22\))

\(\therefore\) \(5m(m - 5) + 3(m - 5) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \((m - 5)(5m + 3) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(m - 5 = 0\) or \(5m + 3 = 0\), so \(m = 5\) or \(m = -\dfrac{3}{5}\)

\(\therefore\) 5 and \(-\dfrac{3}{5}\) are the roots of the given quadratic equation.

\(2x^2 - 2x + \dfrac{1}{2} = 0\)

Multiplying throughout by 2,

\(\therefore\) \(4x^2 - 4x + 1 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(4x^2 - 2x - 2x + 1 = 0\)   (since \(-2 \times -2 = 4 = 4 \times 1\) and \(-2 - 2 = -4\))

\(\therefore\) \(2x(2x - 1) - 1(2x - 1) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \((2x - 1)(2x - 1) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(2x - 1 = 0\) or \(2x - 1 = 0\), so \(x = \dfrac{1}{2}\) or \(x = \dfrac{1}{2}\)

\(\therefore\) \(\dfrac{1}{2}\) and \(\dfrac{1}{2}\) are the roots of the given quadratic equation; that is, the two roots are equal.

\(6x - \dfrac{2}{x} = 1\)

Multiplying throughout by \(x\) (note \(x \neq 0\)),

\(\therefore\) \(6x^2 - 2 = x\)

\(\therefore\) \(6x^2 - x - 2 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(6x^2 - 4x + 3x - 2 = 0\)   (since \(-4 \times 3 = -12 = 6 \times -2\) and \(-4 + 3 = -1\))

\(\therefore\) \(2x(3x - 2) + 1(3x - 2) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \((3x - 2)(2x + 1) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(3x - 2 = 0\) or \(2x + 1 = 0\), so \(x = \dfrac{2}{3}\) or \(x = -\dfrac{1}{2}\)

\(\therefore\) \(\dfrac{2}{3}\) and \(-\dfrac{1}{2}\) are the roots of the given quadratic equation.

\(\sqrt{2}\,x^2 + 7x + 5\sqrt{2} = 0\)

Here \(\sqrt{2} \times 5\sqrt{2} = 10\), and \(5 + 2 = 7\), so the middle term splits as \(5x + 2x\).

\(\sqrt{2}\,x^2 + 5x + 2x + 5\sqrt{2} = 0\)

\(x(\sqrt{2}\,x + 5) + \sqrt{2}(\sqrt{2}\,x + 5) = 0\)   (using \(2x = \sqrt{2} \times \sqrt{2}\,x\))

\((\sqrt{2}\,x + 5)(x + \sqrt{2}) = 0\)

\((\sqrt{2}\,x + 5) = 0\) or \((x + \sqrt{2}) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(x = -\dfrac{5}{\sqrt{2}}\) or \(x = -\sqrt{2}\)

\(\therefore\) \(-\dfrac{5}{\sqrt{2}}\) and \(-\sqrt{2}\) are roots of the equation.

(Filling the book's boxes : the split terms are \(5x\) and \(2x\), the common bracket is \((\sqrt{2}\,x + 5)\), and the remaining root is \(-\dfrac{5}{\sqrt{2}}\), which may also be written \(-\dfrac{5\sqrt{2}}{2}\).)

\(3x^2 - 2\sqrt{6}\,x + 2 = 0\)

Here \(3 \times 2 = 6 = \sqrt{6} \times \sqrt{6}\), and \(-\sqrt{6} - \sqrt{6} = -2\sqrt{6}\), so the middle term splits as \(-\sqrt{6}\,x - \sqrt{6}\,x\).

\(\therefore\) \(3x^2 - \sqrt{6}\,x - \sqrt{6}\,x + 2 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(\sqrt{3}\,x(\sqrt{3}\,x - \sqrt{2}) - \sqrt{2}(\sqrt{3}\,x - \sqrt{2}) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \((\sqrt{3}\,x - \sqrt{2})(\sqrt{3}\,x - \sqrt{2}) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(\sqrt{3}\,x - \sqrt{2} = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(x = \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}}\)

\(\therefore\) \(\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}}\) and \(\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}}\) are the roots of the given quadratic equation; the two roots are equal. (\(\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}}\) is the same number as \(\dfrac{\sqrt{6}}{3}\).)

\(2m(m - 24) = 50\)

\(\therefore\) \(2m^2 - 48m = 50\)

\(\therefore\) \(2m^2 - 48m - 50 = 0\)

Dividing throughout by 2,

\(\therefore\) \(m^2 - 24m - 25 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(m^2 - 25m + m - 25 = 0\)   (since \(-25 \times 1 = -25\) and \(-25 + 1 = -24\))

\(\therefore\) \(m(m - 25) + 1(m - 25) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \((m - 25)(m + 1) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(m - 25 = 0\) or \(m + 1 = 0\), so \(m = 25\) or \(m = -1\)

\(\therefore\) 25 and \(-1\) are the roots of the given quadratic equation.

\(25m^2 = 9\)

\(\therefore\) \(25m^2 - 9 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \((5m)^2 - (3)^2 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \((5m + 3)(5m - 3) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(5m + 3 = 0\) or \(5m - 3 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(m = -\dfrac{3}{5}\) or \(m = \dfrac{3}{5}\)

\(\therefore\) \(-\dfrac{3}{5}\) and \(\dfrac{3}{5}\) are the roots of the given quadratic equation.

\(7m^2 = 21m\)

\(\therefore\) \(7m^2 - 21m = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(7m(m - 3) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(7m = 0\) or \(m - 3 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(m = 0\) or \(m = 3\)

\(\therefore\) 0 and 3 are the roots of the given quadratic equation.

\(m^2 - 11 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(m^2 - (\sqrt{11})^2 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \((m + \sqrt{11})(m - \sqrt{11}) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(m + \sqrt{11} = 0\) or \(m - \sqrt{11} = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(m = -\sqrt{11}\) or \(m = \sqrt{11}\)

\(\therefore\) \(-\sqrt{11}\) and \(\sqrt{11}\) are the roots of the given quadratic equation.

\(x^2 + x - 20 = 0\)

Here \(b = 1\), so \(\left(\dfrac{b}{2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{1}{4}\).

\(\therefore\) \(x^2 + x + \dfrac{1}{4} - \dfrac{1}{4} - 20 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(\left(x + \dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2 - \dfrac{81}{4} = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(\left(x + \dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{81}{4}\)

\(\therefore\) \(x + \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{9}{2}\) or \(x + \dfrac{1}{2} = -\dfrac{9}{2}\)

\(\therefore\) \(x = 4\) or \(x = -5\)

\(\therefore\) 4 and \(-5\) are the roots of the given quadratic equation.

\(x^2 + 2x - 5 = 0\)

Here \(b = 2\), so \(\left(\dfrac{b}{2}\right)^2 = 1\).

\(\therefore\) \(x^2 + 2x + 1 - 1 - 5 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \((x + 1)^2 - 6 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \((x + 1)^2 = 6\)

\(\therefore\) \(x + 1 = \sqrt{6}\) or \(x + 1 = -\sqrt{6}\)

\(\therefore\) \(x = \sqrt{6} - 1\) or \(x = -\sqrt{6} - 1\)

\(\therefore\) \((\sqrt{6} - 1)\) and \((-\sqrt{6} - 1)\) are the roots of the given quadratic equation.

\(m^2 - 5m = -3\)

\(\therefore\) \(m^2 - 5m + 3 = 0\)

Here \(b = -5\), so \(\left(\dfrac{b}{2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{25}{4}\).

\(\therefore\) \(m^2 - 5m + \dfrac{25}{4} - \dfrac{25}{4} + 3 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(\left(m - \dfrac{5}{2}\right)^2 - \dfrac{13}{4} = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(\left(m - \dfrac{5}{2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{13}{4}\)

\(\therefore\) \(m - \dfrac{5}{2} = \dfrac{\sqrt{13}}{2}\) or \(m - \dfrac{5}{2} = -\dfrac{\sqrt{13}}{2}\)

\(\therefore\) \(m = \dfrac{\sqrt{13} + 5}{2}\) or \(m = \dfrac{-\sqrt{13} + 5}{2}\)

\(\therefore\) \(\dfrac{\sqrt{13} + 5}{2}\) and \(\dfrac{-\sqrt{13} + 5}{2}\) are the roots of the given quadratic equation.

\(9y^2 - 12y + 2 = 0\)

Dividing throughout by 9,

\(\therefore\) \(y^2 - \dfrac{4}{3}y + \dfrac{2}{9} = 0\)

Here \(b = -\dfrac{4}{3}\), so \(\left(\dfrac{b}{2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{4}{9}\).

\(\therefore\) \(y^2 - \dfrac{4}{3}y + \dfrac{4}{9} - \dfrac{4}{9} + \dfrac{2}{9} = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(\left(y - \dfrac{2}{3}\right)^2 - \dfrac{2}{9} = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(\left(y - \dfrac{2}{3}\right)^2 = \dfrac{2}{9}\)

\(\therefore\) \(y - \dfrac{2}{3} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{3}\) or \(y - \dfrac{2}{3} = -\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{3}\)

\(\therefore\) \(y = \dfrac{\sqrt{2} + 2}{3}\) or \(y = \dfrac{-\sqrt{2} + 2}{3}\)

\(\therefore\) \(\dfrac{\sqrt{2} + 2}{3}\) and \(\dfrac{-\sqrt{2} + 2}{3}\) are the roots of the given quadratic equation.

\(2y^2 + 9y + 10 = 0\)

Dividing throughout by 2,

\(\therefore\) \(y^2 + \dfrac{9}{2}y + 5 = 0\)

Here \(b = \dfrac{9}{2}\), so \(\left(\dfrac{b}{2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{81}{16}\).

\(\therefore\) \(y^2 + \dfrac{9}{2}y + \dfrac{81}{16} - \dfrac{81}{16} + 5 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(\left(y + \dfrac{9}{4}\right)^2 - \dfrac{1}{16} = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(\left(y + \dfrac{9}{4}\right)^2 = \dfrac{1}{16}\)

\(\therefore\) \(y + \dfrac{9}{4} = \dfrac{1}{4}\) or \(y + \dfrac{9}{4} = -\dfrac{1}{4}\)

\(\therefore\) \(y = -2\) or \(y = -\dfrac{5}{2}\)

\(\therefore\) \(-2\) and \(-\dfrac{5}{2}\) are the roots of the given quadratic equation.

\(5x^2 = 4x + 7\)

\(\therefore\) \(5x^2 - 4x - 7 = 0\)

Dividing throughout by 5,

\(\therefore\) \(x^2 - \dfrac{4}{5}x - \dfrac{7}{5} = 0\)

Here \(b = -\dfrac{4}{5}\), so \(\left(\dfrac{b}{2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{4}{25}\).

\(\therefore\) \(x^2 - \dfrac{4}{5}x + \dfrac{4}{25} - \dfrac{4}{25} - \dfrac{7}{5} = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(\left(x - \dfrac{2}{5}\right)^2 - \dfrac{39}{25} = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(\left(x - \dfrac{2}{5}\right)^2 = \dfrac{39}{25}\)

\(\therefore\) \(x - \dfrac{2}{5} = \dfrac{\sqrt{39}}{5}\) or \(x - \dfrac{2}{5} = -\dfrac{\sqrt{39}}{5}\)

\(\therefore\) \(x = \dfrac{2 + \sqrt{39}}{5}\) or \(x = \dfrac{2 - \sqrt{39}}{5}\)

\(\therefore\) \(\dfrac{2 + \sqrt{39}}{5}\) and \(\dfrac{2 - \sqrt{39}}{5}\) are the roots of the given quadratic equation.

\(x^2 - 7x + 5 = 0\)

This is already in the general form \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\).

Comparing with \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\),

\(a = 1\), \(b = -7\), \(c = 5\)

\(x^2 + 6x + 5 = 0\)

Comparing with \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\), \(a = 1\), \(b = 6\), \(c = 5\)

\(b^2 - 4ac = (6)^2 - 4 \times 1 \times 5 = 36 - 20\)

\(= 16\)

\(x = \dfrac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}\)

\(= \dfrac{-6 \pm \sqrt{16}}{2 \times 1} = \dfrac{-6 \pm 4}{2}\)

\(\therefore\) \(x = \dfrac{-6 + 4}{2} = -1\) or \(x = \dfrac{-6 - 4}{2} = -5\)

\(\therefore\) \(-1\) and \(-5\) are the roots of the given quadratic equation.

\(x^2 - 3x - 2 = 0\)

Comparing with \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\), \(a = 1\), \(b = -3\), \(c = -2\)

\(b^2 - 4ac = (-3)^2 - 4 \times 1 \times (-2) = 9 + 8\)

\(= 17\)

\(x = \dfrac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}\)

\(= \dfrac{-(-3) \pm \sqrt{17}}{2 \times 1} = \dfrac{3 \pm \sqrt{17}}{2}\)

\(\therefore\) \(\dfrac{3 + \sqrt{17}}{2}\) and \(\dfrac{3 - \sqrt{17}}{2}\) are the roots of the given quadratic equation.

\(3m^2 + 2m - 7 = 0\)

Comparing with \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\), \(a = 3\), \(b = 2\), \(c = -7\)

\(b^2 - 4ac = (2)^2 - 4 \times 3 \times (-7) = 4 + 84\)

\(= 88\)

\(x = \dfrac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}\)

\(m = \dfrac{-2 \pm \sqrt{88}}{2 \times 3} = \dfrac{-2 \pm 2\sqrt{22}}{6} = \dfrac{-1 \pm \sqrt{22}}{3}\)

\(\therefore\) \(\dfrac{-1 + \sqrt{22}}{3}\) and \(\dfrac{-1 - \sqrt{22}}{3}\) are the roots of the given quadratic equation.

\(5m^2 - 4m - 2 = 0\)

Comparing with \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\), \(a = 5\), \(b = -4\), \(c = -2\)

\(b^2 - 4ac = (-4)^2 - 4 \times 5 \times (-2) = 16 + 40\)

\(= 56\)

\(x = \dfrac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}\)

\(m = \dfrac{-(-4) \pm \sqrt{56}}{2 \times 5} = \dfrac{4 \pm 2\sqrt{14}}{10} = \dfrac{2 \pm \sqrt{14}}{5}\)

\(\therefore\) \(\dfrac{2 + \sqrt{14}}{5}\) and \(\dfrac{2 - \sqrt{14}}{5}\) are the roots of the given quadratic equation.

\(y^2 + \dfrac{1}{3}y = 2\)

Multiplying throughout by 3,

\(\therefore\) \(3y^2 + y - 6 = 0\)

Comparing with \(ay^2 + by + c = 0\), \(a = 3\), \(b = 1\), \(c = -6\)

\(b^2 - 4ac = (1)^2 - 4 \times 3 \times (-6) = 1 + 72\)

\(= 73\)

\(y = \dfrac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a} = \dfrac{-1 \pm \sqrt{73}}{2 \times 3} = \dfrac{-1 \pm \sqrt{73}}{6}\)

\(\therefore\) \(\dfrac{-1 + \sqrt{73}}{6}\) and \(\dfrac{-1 - \sqrt{73}}{6}\) are the roots of the given quadratic equation.

\(5x^2 + 13x + 8 = 0\)

Comparing with \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\), \(a = 5\), \(b = 13\), \(c = 8\)

\(b^2 - 4ac = (13)^2 - 4 \times 5 \times 8 = 169 - 160\)

\(= 9\)

\(x = \dfrac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}\)

\(= \dfrac{-13 \pm \sqrt{9}}{2 \times 5} = \dfrac{-13 \pm 3}{10}\)

\(\therefore\) \(x = \dfrac{-13 + 3}{10} = -1\) or \(x = \dfrac{-13 - 3}{10} = -\dfrac{8}{5}\)

\(\therefore\) \(-1\) and \(-\dfrac{8}{5}\) are the roots of the given quadratic equation.

Following the flow chart :

Step 1 — compare \(x^2 + 2\sqrt{3}\,x + 3 = 0\) with \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\) : \(a = 1\), \(b = 2\sqrt{3}\), \(c = 3\)

Step 2 — \(b^2 - 4ac = (2\sqrt{3})^2 - 4 \times 1 \times 3 = 12 - 12 = 0\)

Step 3 — the formula is \(x = \dfrac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}\)

Step 4 — substituting, \(x = \dfrac{-2\sqrt{3} \pm \sqrt{0}}{2 \times 1} = \dfrac{-2\sqrt{3}}{2} = -\sqrt{3}\)

\(\therefore\) \(-\sqrt{3}\) and \(-\sqrt{3}\) are the roots of the given quadratic equation; the two roots are equal, as \(b^2 - 4ac = 0\) predicts.
